about: Physics blocks whose maths is a formula (ND3b): each keeps its id, ports and results, and its maths is the Equation below, with a name that says what happens.

references: A uniform sphere: density is mass over volume, ρ = M / (4/3 π R³).
Christensen, U. R. 2010, Space Science Reviews 152, 565: dynamo scaling laws and applications to the planets (c about 0.63, f_ohm about 0.9). doi:10.1007/s11214-009-9553-2

equation.name: How dense the core is
equation.formula: rho = M * f / (4/3 * pi * r * r * r)

f.name: share of the mass in the core

source.text: Christensen, U. R. 2010, Space Science Reviews 152, 565

explain.curious: Earth's iron core is about twice as dense as the rock above it, and that dense, churning metal is where the compass field is made.
explain.science: For a rocky world the dynamo runs in the liquid iron core, so its density is the core's mass over its volume. For a giant the dynamo region is the metallic hydrogen inside about 85% of the radius, and its density can be given directly.

params.description: dipole field at the dynamo surface over the rms field inside (Earth and Jupiter, docs/fudges.md)

references: Christensen, U. R. and Aubert, J. 2006, Geophysical Journal International 166, 97: scaling properties of convection-driven dynamos in rotating spherical shells and application to planetary magnetic fields (dipolar dynamos, the ratio of mean field to dipole field at the dynamo surface). doi:10.1111/j.1365-246X.2006.03009.x
A dipole field falls as r⁻³; the equatorial field B at radius r of a moment μ is B = μ₀ μ / (4π r³). Jackson, J. D. 1999, Classical Electrodynamics, 3rd edn, Wiley, section 5.6.
Alken, P. et al. 2021, Earth, Planets and Space 73, 49: the International Geomagnetic Reference Field, 13th generation (Earth's dipole moment about 7.7e22 A m²). doi:10.1186/s40623-020-01288-x

Connerney, J. E. P. et al. 2018, Geophysical Research Letters 45, 2590: a new model of Jupiter's magnetic field from Juno's first nine orbits (dipole about 4.1 G at the equator). doi:10.1002/2018GL077312
atoms.shown: B_eq = k · B_rms · (R_dyn / R)³,  μ = 4π B_eq R³ / μ₀

equation.name: Field a world's dynamo shows at the surface
equation.formula:
x = min(rd / R, 1)
Bs = k * B * x * x * x
m = 4 * pi / mu0 * Bs * R * R * R

k.name: dipole at the dynamo's top over the field inside

Bs.name: field at the equator on the ground

m.name: strength of the world's magnet (dipole moment)

source.text: Christensen, U. R. and Aubert, J. 2006, Geophys. J. Int. 166, 97

explain.curious: Only a small part of the field made in the core reaches the surface as the familiar north-south dipole, and it fades fast with distance: Earth's field at the surface is about seven times weaker than at the top of the core.
explain.science: In dipolar dynamos the dipole at the dynamo's outer surface is a roughly fixed share of the field inside (Christensen and Aubert 2006); outside it falls as (R_dynamo/r)³. The moment follows from the equatorial surface field. The share is set here so that Earth and Jupiter come out within about 15% of their measured moments.
